You're right about the stress and potential damage that high-impact activities like running can do, but your advice about a 160 BPM heart rate is nowhere near universal - and is dangerously wrong for some people. A person's optimal exercise heart rate is very much dependent on age and other factors. A much better metric is to be in "Zone 1" - around or slightly below VT1 (First Ventilatory Threshold) for most of your cardio time. People with higher fitness levels can add in some training in "Zone 2" (between the First and Second Ventilatory Thresholds), and people looking to achieve certain specific performance outcomes can spend some training time in "Zone 3" (above the Second Ventilatory Threshold). The best general-fitness programs are ones in which the person's performance at VT1 improves. (As you get more fit, you can work harder at the same HR - there are a number of things that cause that, and all of them are good).

That said... if your heart rate at VT1 is around 160 BPM, then by all means train at 160 all you want, but that is definitely not right for everyone.
